predecessors.name: Khazar Khaganate (Khazaria)
predecessors.text: the Don-Donets steppe that Cliopatria's Khazaria shape of 888-895 still covers; the Pechenegs 'driven further west by the Khazars and Cumans by 889' arrive on it

successors.name: Cuman-Kipchak Confederation
successors.text: the Pontic steppe 'replaced' by Cumans and Torks after the weakened Pechenegs; Budjak (Bugeac) entered by the Cumans around 1068-1078

successors.name: Byzantine Empire
successors.text: Paristrion (mostly modern Dobruja), where the Pechenegs had settled as allies and colonists and rebelled in the early 1070s; the survivors of Levounion were settled in depopulated areas of the Empire

ledger.x: 889: the Pechenegs, driven west by the Khazars and Cumans, are on the Pontic steppe.
889: the Khazar steppe and the Pecheneg steppe overlap.
892: the Magyars are pushed over the Dnieper.
895: the Pechenegs storm into Etelkoz and the Magyars leave for the Carpathian Basin.
969: the Khazar state ends, and with it the overlap of the two claims on the steppe.
1043: the Oghuz push the Pechenegs west of the Dnieper.
early 1070s: the Pechenegs of Paristrion rise against the Empire.
29 April 1091: the Pechenegs are crushed at Levounion.
1091: the Pecheneg state ends at Levounion.

wars.name: Rus'-Pecheneg wars
wars.outcome: Wars and raids 'for more than two centuries' (920 war by Igor, 968 siege of Kiev, 972 Sviatoslav ambushed and killed, 1036 defeat under Yaroslav the Wise); the page records no border change, and after 1036 the Horde moved towards the Danube.

wars.name: Battle of Levounion
wars.outcome: 29 April 1091: Alexios I and the Cumans annihilate the Pechenegs; the survivors are settled inside the Empire.

wars.name: Pecheneg rebellion in Paristrion
wars.outcome: The Pechenegs settled in Paristrion rebelled in the early 1070s and were defeated in 1091.

certainty.note: A steppe confederation of eight provinces: no border is given by any page; every edge is approximate.
